why_washington: Washington's EV registration records carry BOTH a postal ZIP Code and a 2020 census tract on the same observed vehicle row, so the observed ZIP-to-tract EV distribution is directly measurable. This is NOT national ground truth: it is direct paired evidence from one state.

scope.exclusion_note: ZIPs below 10 EVs are excluded from the weighted mean because a share vector built on a handful of vehicles is noise. Six ZIPs were excluded because their HUD res_ratio sums to zero (no residential addresses) and one because HUD returned no mapping at all; neither was renormalised.

decision.outcome: HUD residential-address ratio MATERIALLY OUTPERFORMS land area
decision.action: HUD res_ratio becomes the preferred Phase 3 ZIP-to-tract allocation method. Land-area allocation is retained as a documented degraded fallback. Method provenance stays on every allocated row. No plan change is triggered: neither method exceeds the 0.35 acceptability floor.
decision.caveat: Even the winning method misallocates 17.94% of EV mass on an EV-weighted basis in a single state. This selects between two candidates; it does not establish that ZIP-anchored tract estimates are good enough to be called observed. They remain zip_anchored / crosswalked.
